data.label: Hiring Guide
data.title:
5 questions to ask before you
*hire a designer*
data.sub: Don't waste your budget. Swipe to learn →

data.label: Sign #1
data.title: Do you *own the site*?
data.body: Some designers hold your website hostage so you can't leave. You must own your domain and hosting files permanently.
data.fix: Fix: Ensure your contract states you own all design files.

data.label: Sign #2
data.title: Can I *make edits* myself?
data.body: You shouldn't have to call a developer just to change a phone number. You need a site you can easily update.
data.fix: Fix: Ask for a site built on a user-friendly CMS.

data.label: Sign #3
data.title: Is it *mobile friendly*?
data.body: Most of your customers are searching for your services on their phones. If it looks bad there, you lose them.
data.fix: Fix: Test their portfolio sites on your own smartphone.

data.label: Sign #4
data.title: Will you *track results*?
data.body: A pretty website is useless if it doesn't get you calls or bookings. The design must be built to convert visitors.
data.fix: Fix: Ask how they track contact form submissions and calls.

data.label: Sign #5
data.title: What is the *total cost*?
data.body: Hidden fees for maintenance or plugins can add up fast. Know exactly what you are paying for upfront.
data.fix: Fix: Get a written quote covering all ongoing monthly fees.
